concept.title: Events, notes and sources
concept.shortdesc: Record what happened in a life, write down what you know, and say where you found it.

conbody.p: A tree is more than names and dates. This chapter is for the parts that make it trustworthy. You add events, such as a baptism or a home that lasted for years. You write notes. You record where each fact came from, and what you still want to find out.

Each page has a few steps. The examples are the Brontë family of Haworth, and they use the sample tree of that name. To follow them, choose on its card on . shows how. If you removed the sample tree, or you work in a tree of your own, use your own people in place of ours. shows how to add a person.
Two ideas run through the chapter. Say where you found a thing, and say what you saw. A copy that someone typed out is not the register itself, so say that it is a copy.
